title: Long farming possession backed by tax receipts
story_summary: A family cultivated a plot for about 28 years, but the land record still showed a distant relative as owner. The relative suddenly claimed the land and asked the family to leave. The family had paid land tax every year and neighbours had seen them farming.
documents_citizen_had: land tax receipts for over 20 years
electricity bill for the farm well
options_tried: civil suit for declaration of rights
lesson: Year-by-year proof of possession (tax receipts, utility bills, witnesses) made the claim strong. Start collecting these early.

title: Long occupation with no paperwork and years of delay
story_summary: A man lived on and used a small plot for about 15 years on the verbal permission of the registered owner. When the owner's son demanded the land back, the man had no receipts, no written permission and no witnesses. He had also waited many years before taking any action.
lesson: Verbal claims are very hard to prove. Without documents or witnesses the case failed. Gather evidence and act early instead of waiting.

title: Uncle claims late father's land, heirs not yet in the record
story_summary: After a farmer died, his land record was never updated to his children's names. His brother (the children's uncle) began telling buyers that the land was his. The children had all the family papers but had never applied to update the record.
documents_citizen_had: old land record in father's name
options_tried: application to update the land record in heirs' names
written objection to the uncle's claim
lesson: Updating the land record in the heirs' names, with a death certificate and heir certificate, is a quick and cheap first step that blocks later claims.

title: Neighbour moved the boundary fence
story_summary: A homeowner noticed a neighbour had shifted the common boundary fence about two feet into the homeowner's plot. The neighbour insisted the fence was always there. The homeowner had the original sale deed describing the boundaries.
documents_citizen_had: registered sale deed with boundary description
lesson: An official measurement is more convincing than arguments. Ask for it early, and keep the original deed and map safe.

title: Land sold using a forged signature of a deceased father
story_summary: A family discovered that their land had been sold through a deed carrying their father's signature. The deed was dated after the father had passed away. A middleman had arranged the sale and the buyer had already paid.
documents_citizen_had: death certificate showing date of death
options_tried: civil suit to cancel the sale deed
lesson: The death date compared with the deed date was the strongest proof. Act fast once you discover a suspicious deed, and keep copies of genuine signatures.

title: Seller backed out after taking an advance on an unregistered agreement
story_summary: A buyer paid a large advance for a plot under a simple agreement on stamp paper that was never registered. The seller later refused to complete the sale, saying the price had gone up. The buyer had paid mostly through bank transfers.
documents_citizen_had: bank transfer records of the advance
lesson: A bank payment trail and a written agreement helped the buyer recover the advance with some compensation. Avoid cash payments and register agreements where possible.

title: Three brothers disagree on dividing ancestral land
story_summary: Three brothers inherited farmland from their father but never divided it on paper. One brother began cultivating the best portion and refused to share the income. Relations were tense but the brothers still talked.
documents_citizen_had: old land record in father's name
options_tried: partition suit prepared but not filed
key_factors: willingness of all parties to talk
lesson: Mediation resolved the dispute faster and cheaper than court, and the family relationship survived. A written partition agreement should follow.

title: One brother sold ancestral land without telling the others
story_summary: After their parents died, one of three siblings sold a piece of the family land to an outsider without informing the others. The other two found out months later when the buyer began fencing the plot. The sale deed was registered.
options_tried: legal notice to seller and buyer
civil suit challenging the sale for their shares
key_factors: buyer could not show consent of others
lesson: Co-owners who did not agree to a sale could contest it for their share. Document your co-ownership and act quickly once you learn of a sale.

title: Same plot sold to two buyers by a developer
story_summary: A developer sold one plot to two different buyers months apart. Both paid in full. The first buyer registered the sale deed immediately, while the second buyer only held a receipt and an agreement.
options_tried: complaint to police against the developer
key_factors: buyer took possession and paid taxes
lesson: Registering the deed quickly and keeping every payment record protected the first buyer. Always verify the seller's title before paying.

title: Relatives challenge a properly made will
story_summary: A widow left her house to her youngest son through a registered will. Her other relatives claimed she was unwell and pressured when she signed. The son had the will and knew who had been present.
documents_citizen_had: doctor's certificate from around the time of signing
key_factors: medical record showing she was fit
lesson: A registered will with living witnesses and a medical record from the time was very difficult to challenge.

title: Handwritten will with no witnesses
story_summary: A family relied on a handwritten note, said to be the father's will, leaving a plot to one daughter. The note was unregistered and had no witnesses. Other heirs disputed it and asked for equal shares.
options_tried: civil suit to claim the plot under the note
key_factors: no proof of the maker's intention
lesson: A will without witnesses or proper execution is easy to challenge. The land was divided among all heirs instead.

title: Tenant refuses to vacate after the agreement ended
story_summary: A small landlord rented out a shop and the written rent agreement expired. The tenant stopped paying and refused to leave, claiming a verbal extension. The landlord had kept rent receipts and had sent a written notice.
documents_citizen_had: copy of written notice to vacate with proof of delivery
lesson: A written agreement, rent receipts and a properly delivered notice made the landlord's case clear. Keep proof that notices were received.

title: Neighbour built a wall on the family's land
story_summary: A neighbour built a boundary wall that took a strip of a family's plot. The family only noticed when the wall was nearly finished. They had a land record, old photographs, and had not yet taken any action.
options_tried: civil suit for removal of the encroachment
lesson: Dated photographs and an official measurement report showed the encroachment clearly. A prompt written complaint also helped.

title: Wrong name entered in the land record
story_summary: After buying a plot, a buyer found that the land record showed the previous owner's name, or a spelling error in the buyer's own name. Banks refused a loan because the record did not match the sale deed. The buyer had the registered deed.
options_tried: appeal to a higher revenue officer
lesson: Submitting the application with the registered deed and following up in writing, while keeping the receipt, fixed the record quickly and cheaply.

title: Neighbour blocks the only path to a farm
story_summary: A farmer's only access path crossed a neighbour's field. After many years of use, the neighbour put up a fence and blocked it. The farmer had no written permission, but the path had been used for decades.
key_factors: willingness to compromise on a narrower path
lesson: Proof of long use and a willingness to compromise on width settled the dispute without a full trial.
